meta.currency_caveat: DIRECTIONAL ONLY. Cross-platform total mixes accounts that may bill in ILS vs USD. Relative budget shares are reliable; absolute cross-currency dollar comparisons are not. Verify per-account currency in each platform UI before quoting externally.

cross_platform_checks.title: Privacy infrastructure completeness
cross_platform_checks.evidence: Windsor.io is a metrics connector; it cannot surface Consent Mode V2 status, CAPI/Events API server-side configuration, tag firing state, or consent banner implementation. However, one visible warning sign confirms signal pipeline gaps: on Meta, action_values_offsite_conversion_fb_pixel_purchase returns NULL on every campaign row (no revenue/purchase value passing to the pixel), and actions_offsite_conversion_fb_pixel_lead returns NULL on every row despite two active OUTCOME_LEADS campaigns (Webinar-Promotion_YouTubexRiverside and Webinar_LeadGeneration_Website). These nulls are inconsistent with a healthy CAPI + pixel stack. Riverside is an Israeli company serving EU/EEA, US, CA, UK, AU - GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and 20-state US laws all apply. Consent Mode V2 enforcement tightened July 2025; without Advanced mode, 90-95% metric drops in EEA/UK. Microsoft Consent Mode deadline was May 5, 2025 for EEA/UK/Switzerland. Google has EU-targeting campaigns (DE_B2C_Alpha_Desktop, UK_B2C_Alpha_Desktop, UK_PMax_Podcasting_Desktop) spending $177K combined. iOS ATT affects Meta App_iOS_US campaign ($6.8K).
cross_platform_checks.remediation: 1. Open Google Tag Manager / GA4 Diagnostics - confirm Consent Mode V2 Advanced is firing with ad_storage and ad_user_data signals for all EU/EEA/UK sessions. 2. Open Meta Events Manager - check CAPI connection status, EMQ score for Purchase and Lead events (target 8.5+ for Purchase), and deduplication rate. Null purchase value = either no value parameter being passed in the pixel/CAPI event, or CAPI not forwarding the event at all. 3. Open Microsoft Ads - verify UET tag and Consent Mode signals for EEA/UK/Switzerland targeting (deadline was May 5, 2025). 4. Audit LinkedIn Insight Tag deployment and confirm CAPI is connected. 5. For iOS App campaigns on Meta: confirm AdAttributionKit / SKAdNetwork postback configuration. 6. Implement or verify server-side GTM for Google to improve signal durability across cookie-restricted environments.

cross_platform_checks.title: Creative diversity audit
cross_platform_checks.evidence: Windsor campaign-level data does not expose individual ad creative IDs or asset counts, so a definitive count of distinct creative concepts is not possible from this data source. However, structural signals are visible: Meta has 11 active campaigns but one (OrganicPromotion_Awareness) is flagged as quality_ranking BELOW_AVERAGE_35 in the source notes, and the Brand_Love-Campaign_Engagement campaign accounts for $28.9K spend (26% of Meta budget) with a CTR of 0.40% and only 6 custom conversions - indicating heavy concentration on a low-performing creative theme. On LinkedIn, 5 of 18 campaigns have BRAND_AWARENESS objective and share overlapping Marketers/Producers audience segments, suggesting limited creative variation across the funnel. The fatigue note on Meta explicitly calls out Remarket_Visitors_WW frequency at 7.0, 10.06, and 24.47 - ad sets at 24x frequency have almost certainly exhausted any creative variety. Google Demand Gen has 4 active campaigns under the YouTube Ads Account; creative diversity cannot be assessed without asset-level data.
cross_platform_checks.remediation: 1. Pull ad-level creative report in Meta Ads Manager - flag any ad running >4 weeks with the same static image or video. Target at least 5 genuinely distinct creative concepts per audience segment. 2. For the retargeting campaign (Remarket_Visitors_WW) with frequency 24.47, pause or rotate all ads immediately - this audience is saturated. 3. On LinkedIn, introduce at least one Document Ad or Video Ad format into Marketer-targeted campaigns to break format monotony. 4. Audit Demand Gen creative asset library in Google Ads to confirm video + image combinations are used (benchmarks show 20% more conversions vs video-only). 5. Set a Meta Creative Similarity Score check - flag any two active ads with >60% similarity (Andromeda suppression threshold).

cross_platform_checks.title: Platform-appropriate refresh cadence
cross_platform_checks.evidence: Meta retargeting campaign (Remarket_Visitors_WW_Conv_Purchase_21.11) campaign name contains '21.11' suggesting a November 2021 launch - over 4 years without a structural refresh. Ad sets at frequency 24.47 confirm creative fatigue. The Winback_Traffic_WW_24.03.26 campaign (launched March 2024) has ad sets at frequency 9.9-11.8, also well above the retargeting fatigue threshold of 8 (warning) / 12 (fail). On LinkedIn, BrandAwareness_Podcasting_US_Video_TL and BrandAwareness_Marketers_TL campaigns have no date suffix indicating recency; the Sponsored InMail campaign (US_Webinar_UpsellAudience_InMail_Conversation) has zero impressions and zero conversions, suggesting it has not been refreshed or is failing delivery entirely. Google brand campaigns use MANUAL_CPC bidding strategy - appropriate for brand but should be reviewed against refresh cadence for ad copy. Recommended cadences: Meta 14-21 days, LinkedIn 4-6 weeks, TikTok 7-10 days (not applicable here), Google/Bing 8-12 weeks.
cross_platform_checks.remediation: 1. Immediately pause Meta ad sets with frequency >12 in the retargeting campaign and replace with fresh creative. 2. For the Remarket_Visitors_WW campaign, assess whether the audience pool is large enough to justify continued spend - at frequency 24+, the incremental value is near zero. 3. Establish a creative calendar: Meta refresh every 14-21 days, LinkedIn every 4-6 weeks. 4. Investigate zero-delivery LinkedIn InMail campaign (US_Webinar_UpsellAudience_InMail_Conversation) - either reactivate with new content or pause and reallocate budget. 5. Review Google brand ad copy freshness, particularly for the desktop brand exact campaigns running on MANUAL_CPC.

If this is a micro-conversion (page view, time-on-site) rather than a trial start or lead, the $7.41 figure is not comparable to CPL benchmarks. Bing brand CPA of $2.43 and $3.61 are clearly micro/assisted conversions. Generic podcast CPA of $29.41 is more plausible for a trial event.

tracking_consistency.summary: The four platforms are NOT measuring a consistent, value-based conversion event. Each platform optimizes to a different signal: Google to a mixed conversion basket (brand searches, DSA events, app installs, generic signups across 3 accounts), Meta to custom pixel conversions with no purchase value and no lead event firing, LinkedIn to post-view 'Share conversions' (the weakest possible attribution signal), and Bing to 'conversions_qualified' (a Bing-specific legacy label). This means cross-platform CPA comparisons are meaningless - a $45 Google CPA and a $45 Bing CPA may represent completely different user behaviors. More critically, no platform is receiving a revenue or pipeline signal that enables value-based bidding, which prevents tROAS optimization across the entire $3.69M spend. The absence of consistent conversion tracking also creates attribution overlap risk as described below.

issues.title: No purchase value passing to Meta - value-based bidding impossible
issues.evidence: action_values_offsite_conversion_fb_pixel_purchase returns NULL on every campaign row in meta_campaigns.json. This means Meta receives no revenue signal for its Purchase optimization objective. Campaigns running OUTCOME_SALES (Remarket_Visitors_WW, Newsletter_CBO, CBO_Podcasting_US, B2C-to-B2B_LeadGeneration) cannot optimize toward high-LTV customers. The Advantage+ value optimization feature - which requires purchase value - is completely unavailable.
issues.remediation: Pass the 'value' parameter in the Meta Pixel Purchase event and the corresponding CAPI Purchase event. For a SaaS product, this should be the subscription plan value (monthly or annual MRR equivalent). Implement event deduplication with a consistent event_id. Target Purchase EMQ of 8.5+ (email + phone + external_id + fbp). This single fix unlocks value-based bidding and ROAS optimization.

issues.title: Lead event not firing despite active OUTCOME_LEADS campaigns on Meta
issues.evidence: actions_offsite_conversion_fb_pixel_lead returns NULL on every row despite Webinar-Promotion_YouTubexRiverside ($1,841 spend) and Webinar_LeadGeneration_Website ($3,851 spend) running with OUTCOME_LEADS objective. Meta cannot optimize these campaigns toward the Lead event because it is not receiving the signal. These campaigns are optimizing toward a ghost event, likely defaulting to link clicks or landing page views.
issues.remediation: Implement the standard Meta Lead event on the webinar registration confirmation page (or form submit handler). Fire it from both the pixel (browser) and CAPI (server-side) with matching event_id for deduplication. Verify in Events Manager that the Lead event appears in the event list with recent activity before reactivating these campaigns.

issues.title: LinkedIn conversions are post-view 'Share conversions' - weakest attribution signal
issues.evidence: LinkedIn data note states: 'conversions = Share conversions (post-view external website conversions)'. Share conversions count anyone who viewed a LinkedIn ad and then converted on the website within the attribution window - this includes users who never clicked the ad. For campaigns running brand awareness or engagement objectives (72% of LinkedIn spend = $67.5K), these conversions are largely coincidental overlap with other channels' attribution. LinkedIn is claiming credit for conversions driven by Google brand search, direct traffic, and email.
issues.remediation: 1. Implement LinkedIn Conversions API (CAPI) - launched 2025 - to get click-based conversion data with server-side reliability. 2. Configure LinkedIn conversion tracking to track click-based conversions separately from view-through conversions. 3. Set up LinkedIn Offline Conversion Import from HubSpot to pass MQL/SQL/Opportunity events back to LinkedIn campaigns - this enables optimizing toward pipeline value, not just post-view website visits. 4. Until CAPI is in place, treat LinkedIn conversion numbers with high skepticism in cross-platform reporting.

issues.title: Google conversion basket mixes micro and macro actions across three accounts
issues.evidence: Google has three accounts (Brand, YouTube Ads Account, Riverside.fm) each with different conversion action configurations. The Brand account brand campaigns show CPAs of $0.66-$2.43 (clearly micro-conversions or high-volume brand actions). The AppInstalls_Android campaign has conversions_value = 10,538 (equal to conversion count, suggesting $1/install) while AppInstalls_iOS has conversions_value = 0. Demand Gen campaigns show conversions_value of $62 on $213K spend. US_B2C_Broad_Desktop has $8,777 conversions_value on $452K spend. The Riverside.fm account has campaigns with conversions_value = 0 on significant spend (UK_B2C, CAUKAU campaigns). This inconsistency means smart bidding algorithms across accounts are optimizing toward different things.
issues.remediation: 1. Conduct a conversion action audit across all three Google accounts - list every active conversion action, its type, counting method, and whether it is set as Primary or Secondary. 2. Ensure only one macro conversion (trial start) is set as Primary for bidding in each account. Set all micro-conversions (page views, scroll depth, time on site) to Secondary/observation only. 3. Implement value rules or revenue signals - pass Riverside plan value ($0, $15, $24, custom) with the conversion event to enable tROAS bidding. 4. Consolidate accounts if operationally feasible to give smart bidding more signal in a single learning pool.

issues.title: Bing 'conversions_qualified' definition unverified - prevents meaningful Google/Bing CPA comparison
issues.evidence: Bing data note states 'conversions_qualified used (legacy conversions deprecated, returns 0)'. The conversion event mapped to conversions_qualified is unknown from Windsor data. Blended Bing CPA of $7.41 is implausibly low for B2B SaaS trials, suggesting either micro-conversions or a broad engagement event. Without knowing the conversion definition, the oft-cited Bing CPC efficiency cannot be validated against a comparable outcome.
issues.remediation: Open Microsoft Ads UI > Conversion Goals. Identify what action is tagged as the primary conversion goal. If it is a micro-conversion, add a trial-start or sign-up conversion action matching the Google primary conversion event. Update bids and reporting to use the macro conversion as the primary optimization signal.

attribution_overlap_risk: HIGH. Riverside runs simultaneous brand search campaigns on Google and Bing, remarketing on Meta, brand awareness on LinkedIn, and YouTube video campaigns. Users who first discover Riverside via a LinkedIn brand awareness impression, later click a YouTube Demand Gen ad, then convert on a Google brand search will be attributed (at least partially) by all four platforms. Specific overlap scenarios: (1) Google brand search + Bing brand search are definitionally re-capturing users already acquired by upper-funnel spend on Meta/LinkedIn/YouTube - brand CPA ($0.66-$2.43 Google, $2.43-$3.61 Bing) is inflated by upper-funnel investment but reported as independent conversions; (2) Meta's Remarket_Visitors_WW campaign (frequency 7-24x) is retargeting users who first clicked Google search ads, meaning Meta claims conversion credit for Google-initiated journeys; (3) LinkedIn post-view conversions overlap significantly with Google brand search - any user who saw a LinkedIn ad and then searched Riverside on Google will be double-counted. The only way to measure true incrementality is via geo-based holdout tests (Meridian MMM) or platform-native lift studies. This overlap risk is why the cross-platform aggregate CPA is not meaningful without a unified attribution model in HubSpot/Omni BI.

Without a compliant consent banner, all Meta pixel events, Google tags, and LinkedIn Insight Tags firing for EU users may violate GDPR Article 7. compliance_manual_verification.why: Riverside's US ad spend is substantial ($2.39M on Google US campaigns alone). As of January 2026, 20 US states have active privacy laws requiring opt-out mechanisms and data processing transparency. Server-side tracking is now architecturally necessary for compliance. Verify legal has reviewed data flows for all 20 states and that opt-out mechanisms are technically implemented.

compliance_manual_verification.why: Riverside is incorporated in Israel. The Israeli Privacy Protection Regulations (Data Security) 2017 govern how customer data collected via ads must be stored and protected. Cross-border data transfers to Meta, Google, LinkedIn, and Microsoft must comply with Israeli transfer requirements (similar to GDPR adequacy framework). This is especially relevant given the volume of email/phone data that should be flowing into Enhanced Conversions and CAPI.

The generic podcast campaign (bing_search_us_desktop_generic_podcast_exact) has CTR of 1.37% vs Microsoft benchmark of 2.83-3.1% - Quality Score issues may be suppressing impression share. findings.title: Meta purchase value null - value-based bidding completely unavailable across $112K Meta spend
findings.evidence: action_values_offsite_conversion_fb_pixel_purchase returns NULL on every campaign row. All OUTCOME_SALES campaigns (Remarket_Visitors_WW $23.2K, CBO_Podcasting_US $25.6K, Newsletter_CBO $13.4K, B2C-to-B2B $3K) cannot optimize toward revenue. Advantage+ value optimization unavailable.
findings.remediation: Add 'value' parameter to Meta Pixel Purchase event and matching CAPI Purchase event. Pass Riverside plan value (trial = $0, Starter = $15, Standard = $24, Business = custom). Implement event_id deduplication. Target EMQ 8.5+ for Purchase event.
findings.est_impact: Unlocks value-based bidding across $112K Meta spend. CAPI with purchase value + Advantage+ value optimization benchmarks at 22% higher ROAS and 11.7% lower CPA.

findings.title: Meta Lead event not firing - OUTCOME_LEADS campaigns ($5.7K) are optimizing toward a ghost event
findings.evidence: actions_offsite_conversion_fb_pixel_lead NULL on every row despite Webinar-Promotion ($1,841) and Webinar_LeadGeneration_Website ($3,851) running with OUTCOME_LEADS objective. These campaigns are not receiving the optimization signal they were built for.
findings.remediation: Implement standard Meta Lead event on webinar registration confirmation page. Fire from both pixel (browser) and CAPI (server) with matching event_id. Verify in Events Manager before campaign reactivation.
findings.est_impact: Fixes optimization signal for $5.7K currently wasted on ghost-event campaigns. Webinar leads are typically high-intent B2B prospects - correct tracking directly improves campaign ML optimization.

findings.title: Consent Mode V2 Advanced status unverified - EU/UK campaigns at regulatory and measurement risk
findings.evidence: EU/UK campaigns (DE_B2C_Alpha $40.8K, UK_B2C_Alpha $45.2K, UK_PMax $91.7K, google_youtube_uk $64K, google_youtube_de $27.4K) represent ~$269K spend targeting jurisdictions where Consent Mode V2 Advanced is mandatory since July 2025. Microsoft Consent Mode deadline was May 5, 2025. Cannot verify implementation from Windsor.
findings.remediation: 1. Open Google Tag Manager - confirm Consent Mode V2 default and update commands fire correctly for EU/UK sessions. 2. Verify Advanced mode (not Basic) is implemented. 3. Open Microsoft Ads Consent Management - confirm UET fires Consent Mode signals for EEA/UK/Switzerland. 4. Use GA4 Diagnostics 'Consent overview' report to validate signal quality.
findings.est_impact: Without Advanced Consent Mode, 90-95% metric drops in EEA/UK. Advanced mode + Enhanced Conversions + server-side tagging recovers 30-50% of lost conversions. For $269K in EU/UK spend, measurement accuracy is severely compromised.

findings.title: US_B2C_Broad_Desktop: $452K spend at $592 CPA - highest absolute waste risk in the account
findings.evidence: US_B2C_Broad_Desktop: spend $452,395 / conv 763.6 / CPA $592.47. Impression share only 17%, with 80% rank-lost IS - bidding is insufficient for the query volume being targeted. This is the single largest non-brand search campaign by spend and its CPA is 3-6x the B2B SaaS CPL benchmark of $100-$200.
findings.remediation: 1. Pull search terms report immediately - broad match on a B2C query set almost certainly contains high-volume irrelevant queries inflating spend. 2. Add aggressive negative keywords. 3. Either increase bids to compete properly (80% rank-lost IS means most impressions are being lost to budget/rank, so the conversions seen are a small fraction of potential) or restructure to exact/phrase match with tighter targeting. 4. Verify conversion action - a $592 CPA on broad prospecting is only defensible if the conversion is a paid subscription, not a free trial.
findings.est_impact: This campaign alone is $452K of spend at a CPA that is likely 3-6x benchmark. Even a 50% CPA improvement would recover ~$226K in efficiency over 90 days.

findings.title: Meta retargeting creative fatigue: Remarket_Visitors_WW frequency up to 24.47 - audience fully saturated
findings.evidence: Remarket_Visitors_WW_Conv_Purchase_21.11: ad sets at frequency 7.0, 10.06, and 24.47 (90-day window). Campaign name suffix '21.11' suggests November 2021 origin - potentially running same creative for 4+ years. Fatigue fail threshold is frequency >12. OrganicPromotion_Awareness flagged as quality_ranking BELOW_AVERAGE_35.
findings.remediation: 1. Pause all ad sets with frequency >12 immediately. 2. Refresh creative pool with at least 3-5 new concepts. 3. Implement a creative rotation schedule (Meta refresh cadence: 14-21 days). 4. Consider reducing retargeting audience window or expanding retargeting audience size if pool is exhausted. 5. For the campaign dating to 2021, assess whether a full rebuild (new campaign, new creative, new attribution settings) is more efficient than iterative refresh.
findings.est_impact: Removing frequency-saturated ad sets from Remarket_Visitors_WW ($23.2K spend) and refreshing creative can restore conversion rate. Meta benchmarks show 17% more conversions at 16% lower cost with 25 diverse creatives. Current state is the opposite extreme.

findings.title: LinkedIn InMail campaign zero delivery - potential EU targeting compliance failure
findings.evidence: US_Webinar_UpsellAudience_InMail_Conversation: 0 impressions, 0 clicks, 0 conversions, $3,098 spend. Zero delivery with non-zero spend may indicate budget consumed without ad serving, or budget allocated but paused. LinkedIn Message/Conversation Ads cannot deliver to EU members since January 2022.
findings.remediation: 1. Open LinkedIn Campaign Manager - check campaign status, ad review status, and audience definition. 2. If audience includes EU/EEA members, the campaign will fail delivery for those segments per ePrivacy Directive rules. Replace with Sponsored Content or Lead Gen Form targeting the same audience. 3. If audience is non-EU, investigate ad review rejection or audience size floor (<300 members = no delivery).
findings.est_impact: Recovering $3.1K in wasted LinkedIn budget. More importantly, ensures compliance with LinkedIn's EU Conversation Ad restriction to avoid account-level policy risk.

findings.title: Bing severely under-invested at 1.2% of budget despite 29-69% CPC advantage over Google
findings.evidence: Bing spend: $43,051 (1.2% of total). Bing brand CPC: $0.33 vs Google brand $0.44 (25% cheaper). Bing generic podcast CPC: $9.56 vs Google recording $13.49 (29% cheaper). Bing competitor CPC: $4.69 vs Google competitor avg ~$15+ (69% cheaper). Bing blended CPA $7.41. Microsoft benchmarks show 20-35% CPC discount, 73% higher Copilot CTR, and 37% of advertisers reporting higher ROAS than Google.
findings.remediation: 1. Increase Bing monthly budget to 20-30% of Google search budget (benchmark recommendation) - this implies $95K-$143K/month vs current ~$14K/month. 2. Prioritize competitor and generic keyword campaigns where the CPC gap is largest. 3. Enable Copilot chat placement on eligible campaigns - benchmarks show 73% CTR lift and 16% stronger CVR. 4. Implement LinkedIn Profile Targeting on Bing for B2B segments (16% CTR lift, 64% CVR lift, 30-70% cheaper than LinkedIn direct).
findings.est_impact: Scaling Bing from 1.2% to 5% of budget ($185K/quarter) at current CPA efficiency would generate incremental conversions at 30-70% lower cost than equivalent Google spend. This is directional - verify conversion definition quality first.

findings.title: LinkedIn CPM 2x benchmark - audience over-saturation and poor relevance scores on key campaigns
findings.evidence: Blended LinkedIn CPM: $64.42 vs benchmark $31-$38. Extreme outliers: US_Companies+Producers $352 CPM, US_Contacts $1,034 CPM, US_Marketers_Webinars campaigns $242-$272 CPM. High CPM with low CTR (US_Companies+Producers: CTR 1.79%) indicates LinkedIn's auction penalizing low-relevance ads with elevated CPMs.
findings.remediation: 1. Pause or restructure campaigns with CPM >$150 - these indicate audience sizes below LinkedIn's efficiency floor (~50K members) or very low engagement rates. 2. Review audience targeting for US_Companies+Producers and US_Contacts - these appear to be hyper-narrow retargeting lists driving CPM extremes. 3. Test TLA (Thought Leader Ads) format - benchmarks show $2.29-$4.14 CPC vs $13+ for standard Sponsored Content at 1.7x CTR. 4. Consider Predictive Audiences feature (21% CPL reduction per benchmark).
findings.est_impact: Bringing LinkedIn CPM from $64 toward the $31-38 benchmark would improve efficiency by ~40-50%, potentially delivering the same impression volume at $37-47K vs current $93K spend for the same 90-day period.

findings.title: No consistent value-based conversion signal across any platform - cross-platform ROAS optimization unavailable
findings.evidence: Google: conversions_value inconsistent (many campaigns at $0, others at small values that appear to be plan-tier signals). Meta: purchase value null. LinkedIn: post-view share conversions only, no revenue signal. Bing: conversion definition unverified. With $3.69M in quarterly spend, the absence of any revenue signal in the optimization layer means the entire account is bidding for conversion volume rather than conversion value.
findings.remediation: 1. Define a single conversion hierarchy: Trial Start (macro primary) > Paid Conversion (offline import from HubSpot) > MQL (offline import) > SQL (offline import). 2. Pass trial-start value as $0 (or estimated LTV proxy) and paid subscription value as plan MRR in all platforms. 3. Implement offline conversion import from HubSpot to Google, Meta CAPI, and LinkedIn to feed pipeline progression back into ad optimization. 4. This is a strategic project (4-8 weeks to implement correctly) but it is the single highest-leverage change available - it transforms bidding from 'maximize conversions' to 'maximize pipeline value'.
findings.est_impact: Value-based bidding across the full $3.69M spend. Google benchmarks show Smart Bidding with value signals delivers 18% more unique query categories and 19% more conversions. Meta Advantage+ with purchase value delivers 22% higher ROAS. This is the highest-impact structural change in the entire audit.

findings.title: UK_PMax_Podcasting: $91.7K spend at $481 CPA - worst absolute CPA in the account
findings.evidence: UK_PMax_Podcasting_Desktop: spend $91,728 / conv 190.8 / CPA $480.87. Conversion rate 0.41%. Search impression share 13.2% with 76.5% rank-lost IS - PMax is not competitive in the auction. No conversions_value returned.
findings.remediation: 1. Add asset group-level negative keywords via the PMax campaign exclusion list - PMax without negatives will capture low-quality queries. 2. Provide high-quality audience signals (customer match list, converters list) to guide PMax targeting. 3. Set a target CPA in PMax bidding to cap at a defensible level (suggest $75-100 initially based on trial economics). 4. If CPA does not improve within 4 weeks of restructuring, pause and shift UK budget to UK_B2C_Alpha_Desktop (Search) which is running at $62.80 CPA - still above benchmark but far more efficient.
findings.est_impact: Restructuring UK PMax from $481 to a target $100 CPA ceiling would recover ~$73K in efficiency on equivalent conversion volume over 90 days.

findings.title: Google brand mobile WW: 27.2% rank-lost impression share - bidding too low on own brand terms
findings.evidence: google_search_ww_mobile_brand_exact: search_rank_lost_impression_share = 0.2717. CPC = $0.07 - bids are extremely low. Losing 27% of own brand impressions to rank means competitors or other Riverside campaigns may be capturing this traffic at higher CPCs.
findings.remediation: Increase bids on the WW mobile brand exact campaign. At $0.07 CPC, even a 5-10x bid increase would be well below the $0.44 desktop brand CPC. Brand search IS lost to rank should be <5% for any well-managed brand campaign. This is a 2-minute fix in the bid settings.
findings.est_impact: Recovering 27% more brand impressions at minimal cost. Brand conversion rates are highest (18-31% CVR across brand campaigns) - lost brand impressions have outsized conversion impact.

findings.title: Cross-platform attribution overlap risk undermines true CPA measurement
findings.evidence: Meta remarketing, Google brand search, Bing brand search, and LinkedIn post-view conversions are all claiming credit for the same user journeys. Specific evidence: Meta Remarket_Visitors_WW is targeting Google-sourced site visitors; LinkedIn brand awareness campaigns generate post-view conversions that overlap with Google brand search; Google Video/Demand Gen campaigns generate view-through conversions that may double-count with subsequent search conversions.
findings.remediation: 1. Implement a unified attribution view in HubSpot/Omni BI using UTM parameters as the source of truth. 2. Use Google's Data-Driven Attribution model as the primary intra-Google attribution layer. 3. Run a Meta Conversion Lift study on the retargeting campaign to measure true incrementality. 4. Consider geo-holdout testing (Meridian MMM) to measure cross-channel incrementality for budget allocation decisions.
findings.est_impact: Accurate budget allocation across the $3.69M quarterly spend. If even 10% of attributed conversions are double-counted, the true cross-platform CPA is 10%+ higher than reported - with $3.69M at stake, this represents $369K+ in misattributed value.
